resources.string: Every layout that you turn on is its own input mode. Use the 🌐 key or a spacebar swipe to change between them.
Your languages
Add language
Language data
Download data automatically
Get emoji keywords and prediction data for the languages that you use

With this on, the keyboard downloads the small files a language needs, when you add it and when a new one is published: emoji keywords, so emoji search answers in your language, and word-pair data, which makes predictions better. Word lists are never downloaded automatically. With this off, nothing is downloaded until you ask for it on a language screen.
Switch order
Your layouts
Types with the %1$s dictionary
Key layouts
Make your own key grid, or start from a built-in one
Edit, add and delete layouts
Per-app language
Remember language per app
Open each app with the layout that you used there last

When you change language while you type in an app, the keyboard remembers your choice for that app. The keyboard uses that language again the next time that you type there. You can change language with the 🌐 key, a spacebar swipe or the picker. Apps where you selected no language use your last language. A field that requires Latin letters, such as a password box, still overrides this. A field that gives its own language also overrides this.
System language switcher
List languages in the Android switcher
Add each language to the input method switcher of the system

The keyboard registers every layout that you turn on as an Android input method subtype. The \"Choose input method\" sheet of the system then lists them, and you can change between them there. Turn this off to keep language switching inside the keyboard only, with the 🌐 key, a spacebar swipe or the picker. The keyboard then gives no subtypes to the system, and the sheet lists it as \"WM Keyboard\" instead of as one language name.\n\nTo register a language and to make it switchable are two different things. Android lists only the languages that something turns on. Until then, Android selects them itself from the languages of your device, and it usually selects one. On Android 14 and newer, the keyboard turns them all on for you. On older versions, select them by hand in the system settings with the row below.
Show app name first
The label reads \"WM Keyboard · <language>\"

This puts the app name in front of the language in the label of the switcher. Android decides how it styles the label and the app name, such as which one is bold or grey. This setting changes only the label text, not that styling.
Select languages in the system settings
The list of Android. Use it only if the switcher looks wrong
Android 13 and older: select each language here, or the switcher shows only one
Access
Emoji button in toolbar
Open emoji with one press from the top bar

The emoji button stays visible in the top bar, also while the suggestions show. The emoji panel has a tab for each category. You can search in English and Bengali, and in any language that you add a keyword pack for. Press and hold an emoji for the skin tone variants.
Full-screen emoji panel
Hide the toolbar and move the category tabs up, next to a back button

The emoji panel fills the whole keyboard. The toolbar, the emoji row and the symbol row go away. The category tabs move into the row that they leave, next to a back button. Turn this off to keep the toolbar in reach while you select emoji.
Suggestions
Emoji suggestions
Show emoji while you type. The word birthday suggests 🎂 🎉 🥳
Emoji that match appear at the end of the suggestion strip while you type. This works in English and in any language whose keywords you have. %1$s also suggests 🎂.
Press an emoji suggestion
What happens to the word that you typed. Hold the suggestion for the other one

\"Replace word\" changes the word that you typed to the emoji. If you type birthday and press 🎂, only 🎂 stays, as in Gboard. \"Keep word\" adds the emoji after the word: birthday 🎂.\n\nHold an emoji suggestion to do the other one this time. With \"Replace word\" selected, a hold keeps the word. With \"Keep word\" selected, a hold replaces it.
Replace word
Keep word
Type birthday, press 🎂, and only 🎂 stays
Type birthday, press 🎂, and you get birthday 🎂
Skin tone
Default skin tone
For toned emoji in the panel, the suggestions and the search

The keyboard shows toned emoji (👍, 🙏, 🧑…) with this Fitzpatrick tone in the grid of the emoji panel, the suggestion strip and the emoji search results. It also inserts them with that tone. An emoji that you selected a tone for keeps your tone while \"Override with last used\" is on. The first option (✋) keeps the neutral yellow base.
Override with last used
Use the tone that you selected last for an emoji, not the default

When this is on, and it is on by default, an emoji that you already selected a tone for keeps that tone everywhere: in the panel, the suggestions and the search. You select that tone from the press and hold popup of the emoji in the panel. The emoji does not use the default above. When this is off, the default skin tone always wins.
Emoji panel
Grid size, categories, favourites and recents
Grid size
How wide each cell of the emoji grid is, at least. A smaller size fits more columns

The emoji panel fits as many columns as its width allows, and each cell is at least this wide. A smaller size packs more emoji on one screen. A larger size spreads them out, and each one is easier to hit. When the emoji size below needs more room than this, the cells grow to fit it.
Emoji size
How large the emoji panel draws each emoji

The size of the emoji in the grid of the emoji panel, on every tab and in the search results. The cells always keep enough room around each emoji, so a very large size can also mean fewer columns. The press and hold popup keeps its own size.
Return to the keyboard after you insert
Close the panel when you insert one emoji or paste one clip
By default, the emoji panel and the clipboard panel stay open, so that you can select several items. Turn this on to go back to the keys directly after one emoji or one clipboard paste.
History tab
What the first tab of the emoji panel shows
\"Recent\" lists emoji in the order that you used them last. \"Most used\" puts the emoji that you use most often first. The keyboard always keeps your favourite emoji at the start of both lists.
Recent
Most used
In the order that you used them last
The emoji that you use most often come first
Clear recents button
A button on the Recent tab that deletes the recents list
This adds a \"Clear recents\" button to the Recent tab of the emoji panel. It is off by default, to keep the tab clean.
Kaomoji and Emoticons
Two extra tabs: ¯\\_(ツ)_/¯ and :-)

This adds a Kaomoji tab and an Emoticons tab at the end of the tabs of the emoji panel. Kaomoji are Japanese style faces, such as (╯°□°）╯︵ ┻━┻. Emoticons are the Western ASCII ones, such as :-D and <3. Both tabs group them by mood. If you press one, the keyboard types it as plain text. It does not go into your emoji history.
Emoji descriptions
Show the name of the emoji at the top of its press and hold popup

Press and hold an emoji to show its Unicode name, such as \"skull and crossbones\". The name appears above the favourite control and the variant controls. This helps you to see the difference between emoji that look almost the same.
Animated emoji
Send a moving version of an emoji from its press and hold popup

Press and hold an emoji in the emoji panel to see the moving version, and a control that sends it as an image. The images are Noto Animated Emoji by Google, under the CC BY 4.0 licence. The keyboard downloads each one from Google when you ask for it, at about 800 KB. About 880 emoji have one, and the control does not appear for the others, or in an app that accepts no images.
Send emoji as image
Add a control that sends the emoji itself as a picture

Press and hold an emoji in the emoji panel to get a control that sends it as a picture, in the emoji font that you selected. This is useful when the other person has a device that draws the emoji differently, or cannot draw it at all. The keyboard draws the picture on your device and downloads nothing, except one time for the Google emoji font. The picture goes out in the same way as the stickers of the sticker tool. To change that, open Tools, then Stickers, then \"Send stickers as\". The control does not appear in an app that accepts no images.
Emoji keywords
Download or import keywords to search emoji in another language
Emoji row
A row of your own emoji, like Gboard

\"Own row\" keeps an emoji row between the toolbar and the keys at all times. \"Button\" adds a button at the right end of the toolbar. The button changes the suggestion strip to the emoji row. \"Off\" hides both.
Button
Own row
No emoji row and no button for it
A button at the right end of the toolbar opens the row
The row stays between the toolbar and the keys
Emoji row content
Favourites always come first
Favourites
The emoji that you use most often
The emoji that you used last
Only the emoji that you marked as a favourite
Emoji in the row
How many fit across. A higher number packs them tighter

The row divides its width into this many slots and makes the emoji small enough to fit them. A higher number gives smaller emoji that are closer together. When scrolling is off, the row hides the emoji after the last slot. When scrolling is on, a swipe shows them.
Scroll the emoji row
Swipe sideways for the emoji after the visible ones

When this is on, and it is on by default, you can swipe the row sideways to reach the emoji after the visible ones. When this is off, the row does not move. It shows only the emoji that fit, so a sideways swipe cannot move it under your finger.
Emoji style
Emoji font
How emoji look on the keyboard itself

\"System\" uses the emoji pack of your device. On Samsung devices that is the Samsung set. \"Google\" downloads Noto Color Emoji, the standard Android look, one time through the system font provider, and keeps it on your device. \"Installed\" uses an emoji font from Addons, such as Twemoji or OpenMoji. \"Custom\" uses one emoji font file that you import below. The text that you send is always plain Unicode. Other apps and other devices draw it with their own emoji font.
System
Google
Installed
The emoji pack of your device
Noto Color Emoji, the standard Android look
An emoji font from Addons, such as Twemoji or OpenMoji
One emoji font file that you import below
Get the newest emoji
Downloads the current Noto Color Emoji, with the newest emoji in it. About %1$s. The \"Google\" option above can only use the version that your device already has.
Download
New emoji are available
Version %1$s of Noto Color Emoji is out, with emoji that your copy does not have. About %2$s.
Update
You did not import an emoji font. The keyboard uses the system font until you import one.
Replace emoji font file
Import emoji font file
Hide emoji that your device cannot show
Skip emoji that show as a blank box in the panel, the search and the suggestions

Older devices, and some brands, have an emoji font that is older than the newest emoji. Those emoji then show as an empty \"tofu\" box. This setting hides every emoji that the emoji font of your device cannot draw. To see them all, set the emoji font above to \"Google\" (Noto Color Emoji). You can also install a complete emoji font from Addons, such as Twemoji or OpenMoji. WM Keyboard has no emoji font of its own. It uses the font that you select here.

The font that you selected above covers only the emoji that it was built with. Usually only the newest release has the newest emoji. The keyboard does not hide those emoji. It draws each one in the emoji font of your device, so you still see it, but in another style.
Tip: press and hold any emoji in the panel to make it a favourite or to select skin tones. For an emoji with two persons, such as 🤝, you can set the tone of each person.
No emoji fonts are installed. Install one from Addons, such as Twemoji or OpenMoji. You can also import one file with the \"Custom\" setting.
Selected
Delete %1$s
Recent emoji kept
How many emoji the history tab remembers

The history tab lists your favourites first and then the emoji you used most recently. Thirty two is about one row on a small phone and four on a tablet, so raise it if history feels too short. Lowering it trims the list straight away. This setting is 32 by default.
Clear emoji history
Forget recents, usage counts, favourites and skin tone picks
The history tab empties, your favourites are unpinned, and the skin tone picked for each emoji goes back to the default. Emoji themselves are not affected. This cannot be undone.
Downloads on mobile data
Set in Data saver, along with the other downloads
Link romanized languages automatically
Pair a romanized language with the languages it is typed alongside

Adding a romanized language such as Banglish links it with the other languages that share its script, so suggestions come from both. The linking runs every time you add a language, which means a link you removed by hand would come back. Turn this off to keep your own choices. This setting is on by default.
Forget remembered apps
